column1: # gate-ablation-adjudication.tsv — the recorded adjudication (#609 AC-2, D-b).
# The mechanical column is computed; this one is JUDGMENT, and it is the column the demotion
# table ranks by. Every row cites the record it was read from. A gate point with no row here is a
# HARD FAILURE in the generator, so the file cannot go stale as the corpus grows.
# The question each decision answers is AC-2s, verbatim: DID THE DEMANDED FIX ALTER WHAT SHIPPED.
# Not "would the merge have gone the other way" — that is the census slices question and it needs
# the redundancy analysis the report carries in prose. A refusal whose remedy is an act the
# checklist already prescribes (write the spec, hand off the review, post the closing comment)
# altered nothing: the run was going to do it anyway, and the refusal announced an ordering.
# Columns: key <TAB> decision <TAB> false_red <TAB> citation <TAB> note
#   key        a gate point, or `<issue>:<gate point>` to override one run
#   false_red  yes only where a COMMITTED record explicitly contradicts the refusal (AC-4 floor)
#   note       renders as the earn-your-keep tables "what changed" cell
